problem.statement: Solve 2x = 2 over the real numbers. Every displayed Equivalent transformation claims equal solution sets over R; no extra sign constraint is retained.
problem.goal: Judge each claimed equivalence and the final real solution set independently.

conditions.description: The candidate domain is all real numbers throughout the displayed equivalences.

assumptions.description: Squaring must preserve the reverse implication when equivalence is claimed over the stated domain.
The candidate variable is an integer.

methods.name: Equation transformations
methods.description: Follow the displayed sequence over the stated real domain.

steps.explanation: Square both sides, claiming an equivalent equation over all reals.
Take the principal square root and claim equivalence over all reals.

annotations.basis: Division by the nonzero constant 2 is reversible.
x=1 has the solution set {1}, whereas x squared=1 has {-1,1}; the reverse implication fails at -1.
Over R, sqrt(x squared)=abs(x), so x squared=1 implies abs(x)=1, not x=1. This step drops -1.

mathematical_basis: The original equation 2x=2 has exactly the solution x=1.
The first transformation preserves {1}. Step 2 changes the solution set from {1} to {-1,1}; its asserted equivalence is false.
Step 3 changes {-1,1} back to {1}, again through a false equivalence. The two set errors happen to cancel in the displayed final answer.
Thus the final displayed x=1 is correct for the original problem, but the proof chain contains invalid steps; the first is Step 2.
rubric.remediation: After dividing by two, stop at x=1. If squaring is used, label only the forward implication and justify the reverse direction separately.
